references.text: Judah ordered that Tamar be burned because she had committed adultery, which illustrates the ancient practice of burning women who had committed sexual sin, particularly in connection with a father's honor.
Prohibition against defiling one's daughter by letting her commit adultery, linking to the theme of prostitution and the desecration of the family.
A man who takes both a woman and her mother shall be burned with fire, the same method of punishment mentioned for a priest's daughter.
A woman who was not a virgin at the time of marriage was to be stoned because she had committed an shameful act in Israel by committing adultery in her father's house.
Prohibition against temple prostitution among the daughters and sons of Israel, related to the theme of adultery and holiness.
Ezekiel describes God's judgment on Jerusalem as an unfaithful woman, including punishment with fire, as a parallel to the penalty for adultery.
